need: write up a malware outbreak that took the file server offline, for review by the executives
clues: the event is over and the servers are back online
the record must give the root cause and the services that were affected
times must be written in UTC
the write-up should say how to stop the same event from happening again
appliesWhen: an unusual event such as an outage or a security breach must be recorded with its cause, actions, and impact
explanation: An incident report records an unusual event from start to end: date and time, summary, root cause, actions taken, remediation, services impacted, and recommendations.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: give every technician one written, step-by-step way to do a routine task
clues: the task is done several times each week
new technicians keep missing small steps
the text must be plain enough for almost anyone to follow
the steps should describe the process rather than a particular tool
appliesWhen: a routine task must be done the same way every time by following written steps
explanation: A standard operating procedure lists the steps of a routine operation in plain language. It focuses on the process, so the small steps are not missed when technicians are busy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

need: record how a licensed engineering application is set up so the next technician does not start from scratch
clues: only one technician knows the setup steps today
the setup questions are answered differently for each department
the version, the 32-bit or 64-bit edition, and the license details must be listed
it must say which users and devices may have the software
appliesWhen: the steps, version, licensing, and allowed users and devices for setting up one software package must be written down
explanation: A custom installation procedure records how one software package is set up: the version, the edition, the licensing, and who and which devices may have it. It saves time on later installs and passes the knowledge to the team.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

need: make sure a new hire has an account, a computer, and building access on the first day
clues: the HR department has sent the start date of a new employee
the person needs a domain account and an email mailbox
the password policy and the acceptable use policy must be reviewed with the person
a badge for the right areas of the building is required
appliesWhen: a person joins the company or a new role and needs accounts, equipment, and access
explanation: A new-user setup checklist is followed during onboarding. It lists the account, the device, the building access, and the policies to review, so nothing is forgotten on the first day.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: remove an employee's access to company systems as soon as the person leaves
clues: the HR department says an employee leaves the company on Friday
the domain account must be disabled, not deleted
the person's badge and security clearances must be revoked
the company laptop must be returned
appliesWhen: a person leaves the company or a role and the person's access and equipment must be taken back
explanation: A user off-boarding checklist makes sure access ends promptly when a person leaves. Accounts are disabled rather than deleted, clearances are revoked, and equipment is collected.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

need: hold an outside cloud email provider to a stated uptime and response time
clues: the company pays a third party for its email service
the provider must commit to 99.99 percent uptime
penalties must apply when the provider misses its targets
the way performance is monitored and reported must be written down
appliesWhen: an outside provider must commit in a contract to uptime, response times, and penalties
explanation: An external service-level agreement is part of the contract with a third-party provider. It sets the uptime and response targets, how they are measured, and the remedies when the provider breaches them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

need: set the response and resolution times that the help desk team promises to the sales department
clues: both groups are departments of the same company
the sales team wants its tickets answered within one hour
the help desk wants clear targets it can be held accountable to
no outside vendor is involved
appliesWhen: two teams of the same company must agree on response times, resolution times, and quality targets
explanation: An internal service-level agreement sets performance goals between teams of the same organization. It states the response and resolution times so each team knows what is expected and can be held accountable.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: share the fix for a new problem so that other technicians and users can find it later
clues: the problem had not been seen before
the solution took several hours of research
the fix should be searchable by keyword
end users may use it to solve the problem themselves
appliesWhen: a solved problem should be written up so others can search for it and fix it themselves
explanation: A knowledge base article records the symptoms and the solution of an issue in a searchable form. Other technicians and users can then solve the same issue without repeating the research.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

need: see how servers, software, and services depend on each other before a change is approved
clues: the team must judge which systems a server change will affect
the records should cover hardware, software, systems, and even staff
faster root cause analysis is wanted during outages
appliesWhen: the configuration items and the relationships between them must be known for changes and incidents
explanation: A configuration management database stores the configuration items of the organization and how they relate. It shows the impact of a proposed change and speeds up root cause analysis.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: identify each loaner laptop quickly and track when it is checked out and returned
clues: a handheld scanner is available at the IT desk
devices go missing from the loaner cart
each device needs a permanent ID that matches its record in the asset system
appliesWhen: each physical device needs a permanent, scannable ID that links it to its asset record
explanation: Asset tags carry an ID, often as a barcode, that is attached to the device and entered in the asset management system. A scanner reads it quickly, which makes check-in, check-out, and tracking easy.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

need: keep count of a small stock of spare keyboards, mice, and monitors
clues: the stock is small and low in value
a simple spreadsheet is enough
no agent software is wanted on the devices
appliesWhen: only a small amount of low-value equipment must be counted
explanation: An inventory list, such as a simple spreadsheet of item types and quantities, is enough for a small stock of consumables. A full asset management system is only needed when the stock grows large in quantity and value.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: make sure the company does not run more copies of a paid application than it is allowed
clues: the application is licensed per device
the vendor plans an audit next month
some copies may be on computers that no longer use them

answer.item: Software license tracking in the asset management system

appliesWhen: the number of installed copies of software must be checked against what the company is allowed to use
explanation: Asset management systems can collect the software installed on each device and its license usage. Comparing that with the licenses bought keeps the company within its license terms.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: know which employee holds each company laptop so it can be collected when the person leaves
clues: laptops are handed out to staff for home and office work
the HR department tells IT when a person's employment ends
a manager is responsible for the group of laptops

answer.item: Assigned user field in each asset record

appliesWhen: the person who holds each device must be known for returns and terminations
explanation: Recording the assigned user of each asset tells the responsible manager who has which device. When someone is terminated, the device can be identified and collected.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

task: buying new workstations for a department by following the procurement life cycle

steps.do: Identify the need that the new workstations must meet
steps.done: identified the need that the new workstations must meet

steps.do: Obtain comparative quotes from several vendors
steps.done: obtained comparative quotes from several vendors

steps.do: Submit the purchase for budget approval
steps.done: submitted the purchase for budget approval

steps.do: Negotiate the contract and scope of work with the chosen vendor
steps.done: negotiated the contract and scope of work with the chosen vendor

steps.do: Receive the workstations and check that the order is complete
steps.done: received the workstations and checked that the order is complete

steps.do: Approve the vendor's invoice for payment
steps.done: approved the vendor's invoice for payment

explanation: The procurement life cycle starts with the need, then quotes, then budget approval. The contract is negotiated before the order, and payment waits until the goods are received in full.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: send each new support request automatically to the right support group
clues: database problems should go to the database administrators
phone problems should go to the phone team
managers want reports on which kinds of problems are most common
appliesWhen: a ticket must be routed to the right group or counted by type of problem
explanation: The category field groups tickets by kind of problem. It can route a ticket automatically to the right team and shows which kinds of problems get the most tickets.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: show how badly a problem affects the user's work so that urgent tickets are handled first
clues: one user's email client is sending spam to the whole company
another user only reports a slow mouse
the drop-down offers low, mid, and high
appliesWhen: the impact or urgency of a problem must be recorded so tickets can be prioritized
explanation: The severity field records how much the problem affects the user and the business. A high-severity issue, such as malware spreading through email, is worked before a minor annoyance.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

need: record which computer has the problem, with its operating system version and service tag
clues: the user has a laptop, a desktop, and two printers
the ticket may be escalated to another technician
a known issue affects only one model
appliesWhen: the exact device, its model, OS version, and service tag must be known to work the issue
explanation: Device information identifies the exact device with the issue, including its type, OS version, and service tag. Another technician may find that the model or version is the key to the problem.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: keep the user and other technicians up to date on a ticket that will take several days
clues: the fix needs a part from the vendor
the user may ask a supervisor to review the work
daily updates to the user are expected
appliesWhen: the work done so far on an open ticket must be recorded and shared
explanation: Progress notes record each step taken toward a resolution. They keep the user informed and let anyone who picks up the ticket see where the work stands.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

clues: the level 2 technician has to call the user and ask the same questions again
the escalated ticket says only that the PC is broken
the user complains that nobody read the first call
no device or contact details were recorded

answer.cause: the ticket was escalated without a clear issue description and user details
answer.action: Record a clear issue description, the user's contact details, and the device before escalating

appliesWhen: a ticket is passed to another level without the details the next technician needs
explanation: An escalated ticket must let the next technician continue without starting over. Without a clear description, contact details, and device information, the user has to explain everything again.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

clues: technicians spend hours on a problem that was solved last month
the earlier ticket was closed with only the word fixed
a search of the support portal finds nothing about the problem

answer.cause: the solution was never written up as a searchable article
answer.action: Write a knowledge base article from the resolution of the earlier ticket

appliesWhen: a solved problem was not documented where others can search for it
explanation: When a resolution is not documented, the same research is repeated each time the problem returns. A knowledge base article written from the ticket lets others find the fix by keyword.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

clues: a person who left two weeks ago still signs in to email
the HR department sent the termination notice on time
the person's badge still opens the server room
nobody signed off on the exit steps

answer.cause: the user off-boarding checklist was not followed
answer.action: Disable the account and revoke the badge by completing the off-boarding checklist

appliesWhen: a former employee keeps access because the exit steps were skipped
explanation: The off-boarding checklist disables accounts and revokes clearances as soon as HR reports a departure. If it is not followed, a former employee keeps access to company systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 57: Documentation

clues: a ticket was closed as resolved last week
the user is still using the temporary work-around
the user says the final fix never worked
nobody contacted the user before the ticket was closed

answer.cause: the ticket was closed without a follow-up with the user
answer.action: Follow up with the user to confirm the fix works before closing the ticket

appliesWhen: a ticket is closed before the user confirms the resolution works
explanation: A follow-up just before closing confirms that the resolution actually works for the user. Without it, the user may keep relying on the work-around.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: return a firewall to its earlier configuration quickly if a firmware upgrade fails
clues: the change board asked what happens if the upgrade fails
the original configuration has been saved
the steps to reverse the change must be written in advance
appliesWhen: a failed change must be reversed to the original configuration
explanation: A rollback plan, also called a backout plan, lists the steps to return to the original state when the primary plan fails. It is mostly the original configuration plus the steps to put it back.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: make sure every critical system and its data can be restored after a failed change
clues: copies of all critical data must be made before the work starts
the copies must be checked to show they can be restored
it is written together with the steps to reverse the change
appliesWhen: critical systems and data must be copied and verified before any change is made
explanation: The backup plan makes and verifies complete backups of critical systems before the change. If the change fails badly, the systems can be restored to their earlier working state.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: try a new patch on cloned servers before it reaches the production network
clues: virtual machines can be cloned into an isolated network
snapshots let the test run again and again
the primary plan still has bugs to work out
appliesWhen: a change must be tried in an isolated copy of the environment before production
explanation: Sandbox testing puts the change into an isolated environment that matches production, often cloned virtual machines. The plan can be tested and fine-tuned without risk to live systems.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: name one person who oversees the e-waste disposal process and answers questions about it
clues: a new e-waste company is being chosen
the process needs a main point of contact
changes to the process must be coordinated by one owner
appliesWhen: a process needs one assigned owner who is the point of contact for changes to it
explanation: Every documented business process has a responsible staff member who oversees it. That person is the main contact and a stakeholder in any change that affects the process.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: submit a proposed switch firmware upgrade for formal review
clues: the technical testing and the risk review are complete
the paperwork must list the item, the reason, the priority, and the duration
the board will not discuss changes that are not on paper
appliesWhen: a proposed change must be put in writing with its item, reason, priority, and plan for review
explanation: The change process starts with a request form that details the item to be changed, the reason, the priority, the plan, the rollback plan, and the duration. It is presented to the change board for a decision.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

need: explain to the board why a Windows security patch must be installed, with the vendor's article attached
clues: the board asks why the work is necessary
the reason is the security of the operating system
the vendor's documentation describes the flaw that is fixed
appliesWhen: the plan must say why the change is necessary
explanation: The purpose of the change explains why it is needed, for example security, performance, a legal need, or a software bug. It includes vendor documentation such as the knowledge base article for a patch.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: list how many systems and people a change to the ordering system will affect, and when it will happen
clues: the change affects sales staff, customers, and deliveries
the board needs to judge how big the change is
the date, time, and duration must be included
appliesWhen: the plan must say which systems and people the change affects, and when and for how long
explanation: The scope of the change describes the systems, sites, and people that the change affects, and the date, time, and duration. It lets the board see how big the change is.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: judge how likely a change is to fail or cause harm to other systems, and rate it
clues: the server provides a critical organization-wide service
a failure could also break other connected systems
the board uses low, moderate, and high levels
appliesWhen: the chance of failure or unwanted side effects of a change must be judged and given a level
explanation: Risk analysis looks for the chance that a change fails or causes problems elsewhere. A highly integrated system that provides a critical service gets a high risk level.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: get a proposed change approved by stakeholders from across the business before it is made
clues: the group meets every week by conference call
only approved changes may be carried out
members come from several business units, not only IT
appliesWhen: a proposed change needs a formal decision from the stakeholders before it is carried out
explanation: The change advisory board evaluates proposed changes and approves or denies them. Only approved changes may be carried out, which reduces the impact on daily operations.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: have colleagues in other departments check whether a shipping system change could disrupt their own work
clues: the accounting team uses data from the shipping system
the change looked fine in IT's own tests
the IT team alone may not see every effect on other business processes
appliesWhen: people in other departments must check a change for effects on their own processes
explanation: A peer review with colleagues in other departments finds effects that IT may not see, such as a shipping change that breaks accounting reports. Those effects then go into the risk analysis.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: confirm that the staff who use a new application interface agree it works before the rollout is finished
clues: users will test in person or at their own pace
a strict time frame for testing is given
the result is recorded in the change documentation
appliesWhen: the people who use a changed system must test it and agree that it works
explanation: End-user acceptance means the people affected by the change test it, in person or at their own pace, and agree it works. Their acceptance is documented before the change is complete.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: schedule the reboot of a busy server at the time that disrupts the business least
clues: system use is lowest after 10 p.m. on Sundays
a set time frame is already reserved for regular updates
the change is routine and not urgent
appliesWhen: a change must be timed for the period reserved for maintenance when use is lowest
explanation: A maintenance window is a scheduled period, usually off-peak, for regular updates and changes. Scheduling the change inside it keeps disruption to the business low.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

clues: a switch firmware upgrade failed overnight
nobody saved the original configuration
the network was down for hours while staff rebuilt the settings by hand

answer.cause: the change had no rollback plan
answer.action: Write a rollback plan with the saved configuration before the next change

appliesWhen: a failed change cannot be reversed because no backout steps were prepared
explanation: A rollback plan holds the original configuration and the steps to restore it. Without one, a failed change has to be undone by hand, which makes the outage much longer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

clues: a technician changed a server setting without telling anyone
the accounting application stopped working the next morning
no request form or approval exists for the change

answer.cause: the change was made without going through change board approval
answer.action: Submit every change on a request form for approval before making it

appliesWhen: a change was made outside the change management process
explanation: Changes must be requested and approved before they are made, so that their effects on other departments are reviewed. An unauthorized change can break systems that IT did not think about.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

clues: a routine update was installed during end-of-quarter financial reporting
the finance system went down at a critical time
the change calendar was locked for the quarter close

answer.cause: a non-emergency change was made during a change freeze
answer.action: Hold routine changes until the change freeze ends

appliesWhen: a routine change is made in a period when only emergency changes are allowed
explanation: A change freeze stops routine changes during critical business periods to keep systems stable. Only emergency changes or approved exceptions may be made then.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

clues: after an application upgrade, staff cannot find the tools they need
calls to the help desk tripled in one day
nobody outside IT tried the new version first

answer.cause: the change skipped end-user acceptance testing
answer.action: Have a group of users test and accept the change before the full rollout

appliesWhen: a change to what users see was rolled out without users testing it first
explanation: When a change affects how users work, a group of users should test and accept it before the rollout. Skipping this step leaves problems to be found by everyone at once.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

task: making a configuration change to a production server through the change management process

steps.do: Document the purpose and scope of the change
steps.done: documented the purpose and scope of the change

steps.do: Perform a risk analysis and write the rollback plan
steps.done: performed a risk analysis and written the rollback plan

steps.do: Test the change in a sandbox
steps.done: tested the change in a sandbox

steps.do: Submit the change request form to the change advisory board
steps.done: submitted the change request form to the change advisory board

steps.do: Implement the change during the maintenance window
steps.done: implemented the change during the maintenance window

steps.do: Get end-user acceptance and document the change
steps.done: got end-user acceptance and documented the change

explanation: The change is planned and tested first: purpose and scope, risk and rollback, then sandbox testing. Only then is the request submitted and approved, and the change is made in the maintenance window and confirmed by users.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

need: make the first backup of a new file server so that later backups have a starting point
clues: the weekend gives a long backup window
every file must be copied whatever the state of its archive bit
no earlier backup of the server exists
appliesWhen: the entire data set must be copied, and a long backup window is available
explanation: A full backup copies the whole data set and clears the archive bits. It takes the longest, so it is usually run on weekends, and incremental or differential backups build on it.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: make the smallest and fastest backup each weeknight after Sunday's full backup
clues: the nightly backup window is short
only files changed since the previous night's job should be copied
a longer restore that needs several backup sets is acceptable
the archive bit should be cleared after each job
appliesWhen: nightly backups must be as small and fast as possible and a longer restore is acceptable
explanation: An incremental backup copies only the files changed since the last full or incremental backup and then clears the archive bit. Backups are small, but a restore needs the full backup and every incremental after it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

need: keep weeknight backups short while making sure a restore needs only two backup sets
clues: the nightly job must not clear the archive bit
each night copies everything changed since Sunday's full backup
the nightly jobs may grow larger through the week
appliesWhen: a restore must need only the last full backup plus one more backup set
explanation: A differential backup copies everything changed since the last full backup and does not clear the archive bit. A restore needs only the full backup and the latest differential.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

need: get a new full backup each week without copying the whole data set from the server again
clues: the backup software can merge the last full backup with the later incrementals
a restore should need only one backup set
the server cannot handle the load of a complete backup every week
appliesWhen: a full backup must be built from existing backups without reading the whole data set again
explanation: A synthetic full backup is made by the backup software from the last full backup and the later incrementals or differentials. It works as a full backup for a restore without the overhead of a real one.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: put back a project folder that a user deleted from a department share, where it was before
clues: the user wants the files back in the same share
last night's backup contains the folder
nothing else in the share needs to be compared or kept
appliesWhen: data must go back to its original location, overwriting what is there
explanation: An in-place or overwrite recovery writes the backed-up data back to its original location. It is the obvious choice when a deleted or corrupted folder must return to where it was.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

need: let a user compare last month's copies of some files with the current ones
clues: the user is not sure the current files are correct
the current files must stay exactly as they are
the restored copies should be clearly labeled so nobody works in them by mistake
appliesWhen: the restored data must not touch the original location, or the original location is unavailable
explanation: An alternative location recovery restores the data somewhere other than its original place. The current data is left alone, so it is a low-risk way to compare old and new files.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: rebuild a failed server on new hardware with its operating system, settings, and files at once
clues: the server's motherboard failed and the hardware was replaced
reinstalling the operating system from scratch would take too long
the backups capture the complete server
appliesWhen: a complete system must be rebuilt on new hardware from a backup of the whole machine
explanation: An image-based backup captures the complete server, so a bare-metal restore puts everything back on new hardware. It spares the technician from reinstalling the server from scratch.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: let users get back their own earlier copies of a spreadsheet on a file share without calling IT
clues: snapshots of the volume are taken every hour
the user saved over the spreadsheet an hour ago
users should not need a technician for single-file restores
appliesWhen: a user must restore an earlier snapshot of a single file on their own
explanation: Volume Shadow Copy takes snapshots of a volume, and users open the Previous Versions tab of a file or folder to restore an earlier copy. Users can recover single files without help from IT.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: keep daily, weekly, and monthly backups for a year with the same set of tapes
clues: the last backup of each week becomes the weekly set
the last weekly backup of each month is kept for a year
the monthly copies are stored in an offsite vault
appliesWhen: daily, weekly, and monthly backup sets must be rotated and kept for different lengths of time
explanation: GFS uses three sets of backups: daily (son), weekly (father), and monthly (grandfather). Daily backups are promoted to weekly and weekly to monthly, so data is kept longer with the same number of tapes.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

need: protect the sales data against both an accidental deletion and a fire at the office
clues: the live data plus two backup copies are required
the backups must be on two different kinds of media
at least one backup must be kept at another site
appliesWhen: the data needs several copies on different media with one copy kept offsite
explanation: The 3-2-1 rule keeps three copies of the data: the production data and two backups on two kinds of media, one of them offsite. An onsite copy covers deletions and the offsite copy covers a disaster at the site.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

need: use a simple two-week cycle in which each tape is used once before the set is reused
clues: one tape is used for each workday
the whole set is recycled after two weeks
the second Friday's full backup may be archived
appliesWhen: a small set of tapes must cover two weeks of daily backups and then be reused
explanation: The 10-tape rotation uses one tape for each workday over two weeks and then recycles the set. It is simple and gives easy access to recent backups.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

need: restore files that users deleted quickly, without downloading them over the Internet
clues: the office has a slow Internet connection
most restores are single files that a user deleted
the backup device must be physically available to the staff
appliesWhen: fast restores and physical control of the backup device matter most
explanation: Onsite backups on local storage are physically available and quick to restore, with no download from a cloud provider. They are usually paired with offsite copies to cover a disaster at the site.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

clues: the backup software reported success every night
the restore fails after the server drive crashes
nobody had ever restored a file from the backup set
the backup media cannot be read

answer.cause: the backups were never tested with a trial restore
answer.action: Schedule regular test restores and compare the restored data with the original

firstStep: Try restoring the backup to a test system
appliesWhen: backups have never been proven by restoring them
explanation: A backup is not safe until it has been restored successfully; media failure is the most common problem. Regular test restores to a test system show whether the data can really be recovered.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

clues: the full backup from Sunday restored without errors
files changed on Monday and Tuesday are missing after the restore
only the Wednesday incremental was applied after the full backup

answer.cause: the earlier incremental backups were not restored
answer.action: Restore the full backup, then each incremental backup in date order

appliesWhen: a restore leaves out backup sets that the backup method depends on
explanation: Each incremental backup holds only the changes since the backup before it. A restore needs the full backup and then every incremental in order, ending with the latest.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

clues: a fire destroyed the server room
the backup drives sat on a shelf in the same room
no copy of the data could be recovered anywhere

answer.cause: all backups were stored at the same site as the server
answer.action: Keep at least one backup copy offsite

appliesWhen: every backup copy is at the same location as the original data
explanation: A disaster that destroys the data center can destroy backups kept in the same place. Rotating a copy offsite, as the 3-2-1 rule requires, protects against that.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

clues: the yearly restore test passed in January
the tape drive started writing bad data in March
in August a restore found months of unreadable backups

answer.cause: backup testing is not done often enough
answer.action: Test restores at least once a month

appliesWhen: restore tests are so far apart that failing backups go unnoticed for months
explanation: Once a year is not enough for backup testing; at least monthly test restores are recommended. Frequent testing catches failing media before the backups are needed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 58: Change Management and Backup Methods

need: replace a memory module in a desktop PC
clues: the work area has a carpeted floor
the heating has made the air very dry
memory chips can be damaged by a charge too small to feel
the technician will work inside the case for several minutes

answer.item: Wearing an antistatic wrist strap connected to ground

appliesWhen: the technician's body must stay at the same charge as the computer while working inside the case
explanation: An ESD strap bleeds static charge away from the technician's body through a resistor, usually 1 megohm. It keeps the technician and the computer at the same potential while parts are handled.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: set up a repair bench where motherboards and adapter cards are laid out
clues: parts will rest on the bench while they are out of a computer
a part can be damaged just by setting it on an ordinary surface
the bench has a ground point for a cable
several boards will be out at the same time

answer.item: Placing a grounded antistatic mat on the bench

appliesWhen: parts and computers must rest on a surface that drains static charge away
explanation: An ESD mat is connected to ground and drains charge from anything placed on it. A wrist strap can clip to the mat so the technician and the parts are at the same potential.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: store a spare graphics card on a shelf until next week
clues: the card will sit in the IT storeroom for several days
static charges must collect on the outside and not on the card
the card was just removed from a working PC

answer.item: Keeping the card in an antistatic bag

appliesWhen: a part is stored or carried and must be shielded from stray static charges
explanation: Antistatic bags make static charges collect on their slightly conductive outer surface instead of on the part. Keep the bags that new parts arrive in for this use.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: reseat a loose RAM module at a user's desk
clues: the technician left the antistatic gear at the main office
no mat or strap is available on site
the PC is turned off but still plugged in

answer.item: Touching bare metal on the case before handling the part

appliesWhen: no antistatic gear is at hand and the technician must equalize charge with the computer
explanation: Self-grounding drains charge from the technician by touching an unpainted metal part of the case. It is less effective than a strap and mat, but it equalizes the potential when no gear is available.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: install a new memory module and a network card
clues: the technician is already wearing a grounded strap
the parts have exposed chips and gold contacts
touching the contacts can leave oils and static on them

answer.item: Holding each part by its edges or metal bracket

appliesWhen: a part is being installed and its chips and contacts must not be touched
explanation: Components should be held by their edges, and adapter cards by the metal bracket or board edge. This keeps hands off the chips, contacts, and circuits.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

need: replace a failed case fan in a desktop computer
clues: the computer is still connected to the wall outlet
the outlet wiring in the old building has never been checked
the technician's hands will be near the power supply

answer.item: Turning off the computer and disconnecting it from power

appliesWhen: hands will be inside powered equipment and electrical shock must be prevented
explanation: Before any repair inside a computer, turn it off and disconnect it from the AC outlet or use the kill switch. A badly wired outlet can keep a circuit live even when it is switched off.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: deal with a desktop whose power supply has stopped working
clues: the power supply label says it has no serviceable parts inside
capacitors inside can keep a charge after it is unplugged
a new unit costs less than the time a repair would take

answer.item: Replacing the whole power supply instead of opening it

appliesWhen: a sealed part that can hold a dangerous charge has failed
explanation: A power supply is a field-replaceable unit that holds a charge even when unplugged. Replace it rather than open it, and recycle the old one by local rules.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: prepare new metal network racks in a server room
clues: a power fault in the racks needs a safe path to earth
each rack will hold many powered devices
the local electrical code sets the rules for the connection

answer.item: Bonding the racks to building ground with grounding bars and heavy wire

appliesWhen: metal racks or cases must give fault current a safe path to earth
explanation: Equipment grounding connects grounding bars on the racks to a grounded point with thick, low-gauge wire such as 6 AWG. Check the local code, and get an electrician involved when unsure.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

need: set up a new computer next to a wall outlet that sparks when used
clues: the outlet is in the customer's home
the technician is not a licensed electrician
the computer has not been plugged in yet

answer.item: Telling the customer to have an electrician repair the outlet first

appliesWhen: a building's electrical wiring is faulty and must be fixed by a qualified electrician
explanation: Technicians should not repair AC outlets or building wiring. Tell the customer or a manager about the problem and recommend an electrician before going further.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

need: connect a printer whose cable must cross a busy walkway
clues: people walk through the area all day
carts could crush a loose cable
the cable cannot be run through the ceiling today

answer.item: Covering the cable with a floor cable guard

appliesWhen: a cable must cross a walkway where it could trip people or be crushed
explanation: Cables on the floor are a trip hazard. A floor cable guard holds them in place and protects them from being crushed where they must cross a traffic area.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

need: tidy the tangle of power and network cables behind a row of desks
clues: loose cables hang down to the floor
cleaners have tripped on the loops
the cables can be routed along the desk frames

answer.item: Bundling and routing the cables with cable ties

appliesWhen: loose cables must be bundled and kept out of the way
explanation: Cable management routes cables away from traffic and keeps them stowed and tie-wrapped. Cable ties hold two or more cables together so they do not form trip hazards.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

need: deal with a network cable hanging out of a ceiling tile in a hallway
clues: the technician does not know what data the cable carries
network wiring is regulated like other electrical work
people walk under the cable all day

answer.item: Reporting the cable to the network administrator or a manager

appliesWhen: a permanent network cable is out of place and only qualified installers should move it
explanation: Network cables should be inside the walls and ceiling. A technician who finds a stray one should alert the network administrator or manager instead of rerouting it.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

need: get rid of a stack of old CRT monitors and dead laptops
clues: the devices contain lead and other harmful materials
the city fines businesses that put e-waste in the regular trash
none of the devices work anymore

answer.item: Recycling them according to local government regulations

appliesWhen: old equipment must be disposed of in a way that follows the law
explanation: Electronic equipment is e-waste and must be recycled by company policy and local government regulations or ordinances. Many towns offer free drop-off or pickup programs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: write the safety rules for a new computer repair shop
clues: the shop is in the United States
employees will lift equipment and work with electricity
the owner wants the rules to stand up to an inspection

answer.item: Making the safety policies comply with OSHA and other government regulations

appliesWhen: workplace safety rules must meet the law for employee safety
explanation: OSHA requires employers to provide a workplace free of recognized hazards. A company's safety policies and procedures should always comply with government regulations.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: pick up a box of toner cartridges from the floor
clues: the box weighs less than a quarter of the technician's body weight
the box sits on the floor next to the printer
back injuries are a common way IT workers get hurt

answer.item: Bending the knees and lifting with the legs while keeping the back straight

appliesWhen: a load is light enough for one person but must be lifted without straining the back
explanation: Squat close to the item, keep the back straight, and lift slowly with the legs without twisting. Keep the load close to the body.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: move a large UPS battery unit to another rack
clues: the unit weighs more than a quarter of the technician's body weight
a coworker and a service cart are nearby
the path to the rack is long

answer.item: Getting a coworker to help and moving the unit on a cart

appliesWhen: a load is too heavy for one person to lift safely
explanation: An item heavier than about one quarter of your body weight needs a second person. A cart saves trips and strain, as long as it is not overloaded.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: deal with a small fire that has started in a power strip under a desk
clues: the fire is small and has just started
emergency services have already been called
the burning item is electrical

answer.item: Using a Class C rated fire extinguisher

appliesWhen: a small electrical fire must be put out after emergency services are called
explanation: Electrical fires need an extinguisher rated for Class C, such as a CO2 BC or a multipurpose ABC unit. If the fire is too big, leave the building.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: help a coworker who is lying on the floor under a live electrical wire
clues: the coworker does not respond
the wire is still connected to power
nobody has called for help yet

answer.item: Calling emergency services before doing anything else

appliesWhen: a person may be hurt by electricity or fire and no one has called for help
explanation: Never touch a person under a live wire. Call emergency services first; then, if told to, move the wire with a dry wooden stick and give first aid.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

need: blow years of dust out of a dirty tower PC with compressed air
clues: thick clouds of dust will blow out of the case
the particles could get into the technician's eyes
the dust could also be breathed in

answer.item: Wearing safety goggles and an air filter mask

appliesWhen: particles or debris could get into the eyes or lungs
explanation: Personal safety equipment includes safety goggles and air filtration masks. Wear them whenever work could throw debris into the eyes or put dust into the air.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 9: Safety and Environmental Concerns

need: remove a jammed page near the fuser of a laser printer
clues: the printer finished a large job a minute ago
the fuser area runs very hot
the printer also uses high voltage inside

answer.item: Turning off the printer and letting it cool before reaching in

appliesWhen: a part may be hot or charged and must be left to cool after power off
explanation: A laser printer fuser runs hot and the printer uses high voltages. Turn it off, unplug it, and wait about 15 minutes for hot parts to cool.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 59: Safety Procedures

need: get a projector working in the boardroom before a meeting with investors
clues: the executive floor follows a business formal dress code
the technician usually works in the warehouse in jeans
the visit was scheduled a day in advance

answer.item: Dress in business formal clothes for the visit

appliesWhen: the site's dress code is formal and the visit is to executives
explanation: Technicians should match the attire of the environment they work in. Business formal, such as a suit and tie or business suit, fits an executive floor.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: have email fixed on several desks during a normal workday
clues: the staff wear polo shirts and slacks
the office has no formal dress code
the technician has a suit available

answer.item: Wear business casual clothes for the visit

appliesWhen: an ordinary office visit calls for neat clothing without a suit
explanation: Business casual, such as slacks with a collared shirt or blouse, fits day-to-day office work. Overdressing can make the customer see the technician as out of touch with their needs.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: understand why the home Wi-Fi keeps dropping
clues: the customer says he is not technical
the cause is interference on a crowded wireless channel
he asked for an explanation he can follow

answer.item: Explain the cause in plain words without jargon or acronyms

appliesWhen: a nontechnical customer needs an explanation they can understand
explanation: Speak clearly and avoid jargon, acronyms, and slang with nontechnical customers. Heavy jargon can make a technician seem insecure rather than skilled.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: recover a laptop that will not start the day before a deadline
clues: the customer says the situation is hopeless
she is afraid all her files are gone
the technician has fixed this fault many times

answer.item: Stay calm and positive and assure her the problem will be solved

appliesWhen: a worried customer needs to see confidence that the problem can be fixed
explanation: A technician should keep a positive attitude and project confidence even when the customer is frustrated. Calm assurance helps the customer trust the repair.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: describe a printing problem that has gone on for a week
clues: the customer starts a long, detailed story
the technician thinks the cause is clear after one sentence
details later in the story could point to another cause

answer.item: Listen without interrupting and take notes

appliesWhen: the customer is still describing the problem and the details matter
explanation: Active listening means letting the customer finish, writing down key points, and not interrupting. The full story often holds clues to the real cause.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: have a new monitor installed in her office
clues: she introduced herself as Dr. Amina Patel
staff at the site address one another by professional title
this is the technician's first visit to the site

answer.item: Address the customer by her professional title

appliesWhen: the customer uses a professional title and the culture of the site expects it
explanation: Being culturally sensitive includes using appropriate professional titles and designations. It shows respect for the customer's position and background.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

need: explain a scanner fault to the technician over the phone
clues: the customer speaks English as a second language
the technician did not understand part of the description
a misunderstanding could lead to the wrong repair

answer.item: Kindly ask the customer to repeat the part that was unclear

appliesWhen: there is a language barrier and the technician did not understand
explanation: If there is a language barrier, kindly ask the customer to repeat themselves. Make sure both sides understand each other and work toward the same goal.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

need: have a docking station replaced at a 10 a.m. appointment
clues: the technician is stuck in traffic
the technician will arrive about 30 minutes late
the customer has another meeting an hour after the appointment

answer.item: Call the customer, apologize, and give a new arrival time

appliesWhen: the technician will miss an agreed arrival time
explanation: Be punctual, and if you will be late, contact the customer, say so, and apologize. Waiting without notice can make the visit difficult before it starts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: get a slow PC fixed during the lunch break
clues: the technician's phone rings with a personal call
the customer is watching the repair
the call is not an emergency

answer.item: Let the call go to voicemail and keep working

appliesWhen: a personal call or message arrives while the technician is with a customer
explanation: Avoid distractions such as personal calls, texts, and social media while with a customer. Screen calls and let them go to voicemail unless it is an emergency.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: have a point-of-sale terminal repaired at the front counter
clues: another customer calls the technician about a different job
the technician is in the middle of the current repair
no coworker is free to take the other call

answer.item: Tell the caller you are with a customer and will call back shortly

appliesWhen: another customer calls while the technician is working with someone else
explanation: If other customers call, explain that you are with a customer and will call them back soon. The customer in front of you should feel they have your full attention.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

need: get a crashed sales database server running again
clues: the manager is shouting at the technician
he blames the IT department for the outage
the technician did not cause the problem

answer.item: Stay calm, let him vent, and do not argue or get defensive

appliesWhen: an upset customer is angry and the technician must avoid conflict
explanation: Never argue with a customer or take a defensive stance. Let them vent, stay calm, and focus on fixing the problem; the goal is to keep the customer, not to win.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: fix a mouse pointer that jumps around the screen
clues: the fault looks minor to the technician
the customer says it ruins her work every day
she has reported it twice before

answer.item: Treat the problem as seriously as the customer does

appliesWhen: the problem seems small to the technician but matters a lot to the customer
explanation: Avoid dismissing customer issues, however simple they seem. Facial expressions and body language should also show that the problem is taken seriously.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: find out why a laptop stopped connecting to the network
clues: the technician suspects the user changed a setting
the user seems embarrassed
accusing questions can make users defensive

answer.item: Avoid blaming the user and ask what happened before it stopped

appliesWhen: user error is possible but blame would make the customer defensive
explanation: Avoid being judgmental about possible user error. Questions such as 'What did you do?' sound like accusations, so use neutral wording that focuses on the fix.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: get help with a computer that she says acts weird
clues: the customer cannot say exactly what is wrong
yes or no questions have not narrowed the problem
the technician needs more detail to start

answer.item: Ask open-ended questions, such as when it last worked correctly

appliesWhen: a vague complaint must be narrowed down to a clear problem
explanation: Open-ended questions such as 'When was the last time it worked?' help narrow the scope of the issue. They also keep the customer relaxed.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: have an email problem fixed after a long phone description
clues: the customer's description was long and somewhat confusing
the technician wants both sides to agree on the problem
work has not started yet

answer.item: Restate the issue back to the customer to verify understanding

appliesWhen: the technician has heard the problem and must confirm it was understood
explanation: Clarify customer statements by repeating the problem back in your own words. Restating the issue confirms that everyone understands it before work starts.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

need: keep the details of a tense service call out of public view
clues: the technician had a hard visit with a rude client yesterday
the technician wants to vent about it online
the client is a well-known local firm

answer.item: Keep the details private and do not post about them on social media

appliesWhen: the technician is tempted to share work experiences with others
explanation: Use discretion when discussing experiences with customers. Posting about work on social media is unprofessional and could lead to legal action or termination.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: know when a laptop sent in for repair will be ready
clues: a replacement screen must be ordered
parts usually arrive in three days
the customer needs the laptop for a trip

answer.item: Give a realistic timeline and send regular status updates

appliesWhen: the customer needs to know how long a job will take and how it is going
explanation: Once the problem is clear, set a reasonable timeline and keep the customer informed with updates. Allow extra time, and give a new estimate if the job runs longer.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: decide what to do with a laptop that has a failed motherboard
clues: the repair costs almost as much as a new laptop
the laptop is out of warranty
the customer has not set a budget

answer.item: Offer repair and replacement options with their costs

appliesWhen: there is more than one way to solve the problem and the customer should choose
explanation: Setting expectations includes offering repair or replacement options as needed. The customer can then make an informed choice.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: be sure last week's network printer repair really solved the problem
clues: the job was closed five days ago
the user has not reported any new trouble
the fault had come back once before

answer.item: Follow up with the user to verify satisfaction

appliesWhen: a job is finished and the technician must check later that the customer is satisfied
explanation: After the job, follow up with the customer at a later date to verify that everything still works and they are satisfied. It is the most overlooked step and builds trust quickly.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: know exactly what work was done on the file server
clues: the technician replaced two drives and updated the firmware
company policy requires a record of all services
the customer will be billed for the parts

answer.item: Provide written documentation of the services performed

appliesWhen: the work is done and the customer needs a record of what was done
explanation: Be clear about company policies and provide proper documentation on the services provided. A written record supports billing and later support.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: have a printer serviced in the human resources office
clues: printed payroll reports are lying in the output tray
the technician must reach the tray to work
the papers belong to the customer

answer.item: Ask the customer to move the confidential papers first

appliesWhen: confidential printed material is in the work area
explanation: Do not look at or touch confidential materials on a desk or printer. Ask the customer to move them to an area where you cannot see them.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism

need: have a slow PC tuned while she stays at her desk
clues: bank statements and legal documents are open on the screen
the technician needs to use the PC for the repair
the customer is sitting next to the technician

answer.item: Ask the customer to close the private documents before you start

appliesWhen: private information is shown on a computer the technician must use
explanation: Do not look at confidential information located on a computer. Have the customer close or move it so it stays private while you work.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 61: Incident Response, Communication, and Professionalism; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 10: Documentation and Professionalism

need: control the full desktop of a Windows 11 Pro PC in another building
clues: remote connections are allowed in System Properties on that PC
the technician has an account on that PC
the firewall on that PC allows TCP port 3389
no user needs to accept the session
appliesWhen: a technician must take over the graphical desktop of a Windows computer without an invitation
explanation: Remote Desktop Connection, or mstsc, uses RDP on TCP port 3389 to show and control a Windows desktop. Home editions can only be the client side.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

need: get help from the help desk while she watches the fix on her screen
clues: the user must invite the technician
the invitation will be sent by email
the PC allows assistance connections and remote control
appliesWhen: a user must invite a technician to view and control their session
explanation: Remote Assistance lets a user send an invitation so a technician can view and control the user's own session. Remote Desktop, by contrast, connects without an invitation.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: get help with an app error on a home Windows 11 PC
clues: the PC is behind a home router and firewall
the technician will give the user a six-digit code
no third-party software may be installed
the user can choose view only or full control
appliesWhen: a home user needs built-in screen sharing help that works through routers and firewalls
explanation: Quick Assist is built into Windows 11 and connects with a six-digit code that is valid for 10 minutes. It works behind routers and firewalls but has no file transfer.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

need: run administrative scripts on an Ubuntu server from the command line
clues: the server has no graphical desktop installed
the session must be encrypted
the server accepts connections on TCP port 22
appliesWhen: a technician needs an encrypted text console on a Linux or UNIX system
explanation: Secure Shell gives an encrypted command-line session on TCP port 22. OpenSSH and PuTTY are common clients, and the SSH service must run on the target.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

need: control the desktops of a Linux workstation and a Mac from a Windows laptop
clues: the tool must work across several operating systems
an open source protocol is preferred
a server component will be installed on each remote host
appliesWhen: a graphical desktop must be shared across many operating systems with an open protocol
explanation: Virtual Network Computing is an open, client-server remote control protocol, normally on TCP port 5900. It is not encrypted by default, so add encryption or a VPN.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

need: reach the file server at the office from a hotel room
clues: the hotel Wi-Fi is public and untrusted
the laptop must get an internal company address
all traffic to the office must be encrypted in a tunnel
appliesWhen: one remote user must join the company network securely over the Internet
explanation: A client-to-site VPN builds an encrypted tunnel from the laptop to the VPN concentrator. The laptop gets an internal address and works as if it were on the company network.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: connect a branch office network to headquarters over the Internet
clues: the company wants to drop its leased line
each location has a VPN concentrator
every user at the branch needs access, not just one laptop
appliesWhen: two whole networks must be joined securely over the Internet
explanation: A site-to-site VPN ties two locations together with a tunnel between VPN concentrators. It is cheaper and more scalable than leased lines.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

need: watch patch levels, disk space, and antivirus status on 500 client PCs at many sites
clues: an agent will report back from each PC
the managed service provider wants one dashboard for all customers
alerts must arrive when a major change is found
appliesWhen: many endpoints across sites must be monitored and managed from one console
explanation: Remote monitoring and management software uses agents to report security, hardware, and application data to one console. Managed service providers use it to maintain many customers.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: open the console of virtual desktops hosted on a Proxmox server
clues: users connect to VDI desktops
keyboard, audio, and video must work as if they were local
the protocol must be built for virtual machines
appliesWhen: users need rich remote access to virtual machine desktops
explanation: The Simple Protocol for Independent Computing Environments is an open protocol for reaching virtual desktops. It supports TLS channels and Kerberos authentication.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: run PowerShell commands on 40 Windows servers at once
clues: no graphical session is needed
the protocol is based on WS-Management and SOAP
the traffic will use HTTP or HTTPS ports
appliesWhen: commands and scripts must run remotely on many Windows systems
explanation: Windows Remote Management runs commands and PowerShell scripts on remote Windows systems over ports 80 and 443. It must be enabled and configured on each target first.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies; CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

need: run a training session where many staff watch one shared screen
clues: attendees will join from their homes
calendar invites and call-in numbers are needed
more than 30 people will attend
appliesWhen: many people must join a meeting and see a shared screen
explanation: Videoconferencing software such as Teams, Webex, or Zoom shares a screen with many people at once. It adds calendar invites, call-in numbers, and attendee management.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: send a large installer to a user who is getting help through Quick Assist
clues: the screen-sharing tool in use has no file transfer
the file is too large for email
the user will download it from a link

answer.item: File transfer software such as OneDrive

appliesWhen: files must move between users and the screen-sharing tool cannot do it
explanation: Quick Assist has no file transfer utility, so files go through a sharing service. File transfer software such as OneDrive, Dropbox, or Google Drive shares files both ways.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

need: connect to unattended store PCs at any time with no one present
clues: an agent on each PC waits for incoming connections
the tool must integrate with Intune
the console should show which devices are online
appliesWhen: unattended computers must accept support connections at any time
explanation: Screen-sharing tools such as TeamViewer or Splashtop act as desktop management software when installed to wait for incoming connections. They can integrate with Intune or Jamf.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence

need: make Remote Desktop connections to satellite office PCs harder to attack
clues: the PCs accept RDP sessions
users must be checked before a full session starts
the setting is on by default but was turned off
appliesWhen: Remote Desktop users must authenticate before a session is created
explanation: Network Level Authentication requires the user's credentials before an RDP session starts. Pair it with strong passwords, and a VPN for connections across the Internet.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: let administrators reach office PCs by RDP from home without exposing port 3389 to the Internet
clues: the connections cross the public Internet
the company already has a VPN concentrator
attackers scan for open remote desktop ports

answer.item: Running the RDP sessions through a VPN tunnel

appliesWhen: a remote control protocol must not be reachable directly from the Internet
explanation: Running RDP or SSH through a VPN adds an encrypted tunnel and keeps the remote access port off the Internet. Use it especially when connecting across the Internet.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: change switch settings remotely while sending admin passwords
clues: the current tool sends everything in plain text
the switch supports encrypted shell sessions
passwords and settings will cross the network
appliesWhen: passwords or settings would cross the network unencrypted
explanation: Telnet is not encrypted and is fine only for harmless data such as sensor readings. Passwords and configuration should use an encrypted protocol such as SSH.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: copy configuration files to a remote Linux server
clues: plain FTP would send the files unencrypted
the server already accepts encrypted shell logins
the files hold passwords

answer.item: Using SCP or SFTP over SSH

appliesWhen: files must be moved across the network without sending them in plain text
explanation: SCP and SFTP run over SSH on port 22 and encrypt the files in transit. FTP is not secure and sends data in plain text.
source: CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: protect PCs that run a remote support agent exposed to the Internet
clues: attackers can exploit agents that wait for connections
passwords alone have been guessed before
the vendor supports a second sign-in factor

answer.item: Keeping the agent updated and turning on multifactor authentication

appliesWhen: an always-listening remote access agent is exposed to the Internet
explanation: An agent that waits for connections and faces the Internet is a target for attackers. Keep the software up to date and use multifactor authentication where it is available.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence; CompTIA A+ Core 1 and Core 2 Exam Cram, 2nd ed. – Chapter 64: Remote Access Technologies

need: stop strangers from joining the company's online meetings
clues: outsiders have guessed meeting IDs before
the meetings use a videoconferencing service
a recent meeting was disrupted by trolls

answer.item: Requiring a password to join each meeting

appliesWhen: outsiders could guess a meeting ID and join a private videoconference
explanation: Requiring a password to join a meeting stops conference bombing, also called Zoombombing. Without it, anyone who guesses the meeting ID can join.
source: CompTIA A+ Complete Study Guide (Docter) – Core 2 Chapter 8: Scripting, Remote Access, and Artificial Intelligence
